  2. Supernova (Adds the number of times poker hand has been played this run to Mult)
  3. Popcorn [current value 20.0] (+20 Mult -4 Mult per round played)
  4. Mystic Summit (+15 Mult when 0 discards remaining)
  5. Obelisk [rental; current value 1.7999999999999998] (This Joker gains X0.2 Mult per consecutive hand played without playing your most played poker hand)

CONSUMABLES: none

HAND LEVELS (level, times played): High Card lvl 1 (7x), Pair lvl 2 (7x), Two Pair lvl 3 (7x), Three of a Kind lvl 2 (1x), Straight lvl 1 (2x), Flush lvl 1 (4x)

CURRENT STYLE: none

ESTIMATE (the round player, over many possible draws): playing on clears this blind about 73% of the time.

YOUR PLAN NOTE: Emergency: The Needle reads 10%, ante 6 reads 0%, and the only xMult is a small Obelisk. I'm playing the Big Blind (~$41 plus payout). In the Big Blind shop, buy Director's Cut first if it's offered ($10) to reroll The Needle. After that, use 1-2 $5 rerolls or a Buffoon pack to find a real every-hand xMult, keeping about $12+ for the boss shop. To make room, sell Popcorn first (it decays), then Supernova. Buy Uranus or Mercury cheaply if offered (Two Pair is level 3). Against The Needle: use both discards first so Mystic Summit fires, then play the single biggest hand. No second rental unless it is an every-hand xMult.

LEGAL MOVES:
0. Play on: the round player makes the next play or discard (following your style)

Answer with your reasoning, the move number, the target card numbers (for a tarot or spectral that needs them, else []) and the style for the rest of the round.

answer.reasoning: The Big Blind reads 73%, below the 95% bar, so there are no grow goals: the round player should score as much as possible each hand. I'm not setting a hand style either. Pair, Two Pair and High Card are tied at 7 plays each, so Obelisk will mostly look after itself, and it's best to let the round player pick the biggest scoring play. There are no consumables to use.

summaries: The run died in ante 3 with only 2 of its 5 joker slots filled: Mad Joker, which only scores on Two Pair, and Onyx Agate, a perishable joker that was running out. It never had an xMult joker. From ante 2 onward the outlook kept saying ante 3's boss and ante 4 were at 0-25%, but the strategist kept treating the money it held as untouchable. It left five shops without a joker, rerolled only once all run, and spent $20 on Director's Cut and one boss reroll instead of on scoring. What decided it was that money that should have gone into a board went into banking and blind manipulation.

The run died at The Eye in ante 3, which its own outlook put at 64% to beat. The real cause came earlier. Ante 1 ended with a single conditional joker (Greedy) even though the strategist had $14-23 in the shops. That left the ante 2 boss reading 5%, and the run spent the rest of the game in panic mode: about $22 on rerolls, an eternal conditional Hack, and two eternal rentals (Bootstraps and Shoot the Moon). Bootstraps scales with money and the rentals cost $6 a round, so by ante 3 the board was at $5-8 and every purchase lowered the score. All 5 slots were taken by eternals, there was no xMult, and Pair was only level 2.

The run died at the ante 5 Big Blind (37,500) with -$5, two rentals, no real xMult apart from a decaying rental Ramen, and Pair stuck at level 3 since ante 2. The money collapse decided it. The bank never reached $25 and earned almost no interest after the first ante 2 shop, where $22 went to $3 on a reroll and two Celestial packs. Every shop after that was a $1-11 survival scramble that could only afford rentals. That got worse because an eternal Shortcut was taken on an empty board. It locked a slot on a Straight plan that was dropped one ante later, and with the other eternals it left no room to convert the board.

The run died to The Water (ante 4 boss, no discards) after 11 blinds. The board had no real engine: flat +Mult/chips, a shrinking Ramen and an unreliable Trio, with the main hand at only level 3. The deeper cause was money. The run had $27 at the start of ante 2 but never held $25 again. It lost about $15 to rent on a perishable rental Mystic Summit, spent on packs and jokers that did nothing (an unopened Buffoon pick, Superposition), and spread its few planets over Two Pair, Pair and Three of a Kind. In the shop the boss read 95-97%, but once the round started it read 55%, and the run had neither the cash nor the multiplier to cover that gap.

The run got through antes 1-2 easily but never settled on one main hand. It put Saturn into Straight with no enabler, then built Pair jokers, and spent about $22 on five Celestial packs that gave Two Pair/Flush planets. It skipped a blind for a Rare Tag, then left the free Blueprint in the shop. At ante 4 it bought Hieroglyph as a panic move. That cost $10 and a hand every round, so the replayed ante 3 dropped to about 17-30%. The money ran out ($2) and the run died to The Fish. What decided it: no focused hand levels, and no second multiplier when one was offered free.
text:
LESSONS FROM OUR GAMES (version 12; each seen in at least 2 games, most supported first)
- Main-hand levels are the second engine (+6 levels is about +1.3 blinds).
- Choose the main hand by how often you can draw it with 2 discards: you should be able to draw it in 3 of 4 hands. How often you have played it does not decide the choice, unless you own Telescope (its pack planet goes to your most played hand). Your levels must also match the hand the round player really plays. If by ante 2 it mostly plays a different drawable hand (Two Pair played 5 times while Pair was 'the plan'), do one of two things: lock the style to the main hand, or level the hand it is playing (Uranus counts). Doing neither is the failure. Never flip the style back and forth between Pair and Two Pair, or between Pair and Straight.
- Pair is the default once the board has +Mult or chips jokers. It is always drawable, and Sly, Jolly, Duo, Half Joker and Mercury support it. On a blank board (no jokers), Pair is not the plan; see the in-blind pace rule. Leave Pair only for a real signal: Spare Trousers, or a hand-type joker plus a steady supply of that hand's planets. A single common +Mult joker for another hand is not a signal, and neither is one off-plan planet from a pack. Two Uranus bought because of a lone Mad Joker, and Square Joker pulling a run onto Two Pair, both starved Pair. If you buy a hand-conditional xMult (The Trio), change the style and the planets to match it, or skip it. An eternal Trio on an unthinned deck saw 16 Two Pairs for every 2 trips.
- Use Full House, Straight or Flush only with a real enabler. Never level Straight (Saturn) without Shortcut or Four Fingers.
- Commit by the end of ante 1-2 (by the first Buffoon pick at the latest), and make sure the round player actually plays that hand. Once the main hand is named, buy only its planets and jokers that score it. Do not let a joker (Runner, Square, Mad) pull plays toward another hand, or spread plays over Full House, Two Pair and High Card. If the jokers you own really support a different hand, switch to that hand by ante 3 at the latest and stop buying the old hand's planets. One run had Pair levelled but played 0 times by ante 4, while Clever, Uranus and Earth were bought for other hands. Another reached ante 4 with Pair 1, Two Pair 2, Straight 4 and Flush 2. Both failed.
- Take every planet for the main hand (Mercury whenever it is offered). Do not spend money on off-plan planets. Exception: when a pack you already opened (free or paid) has no main-hand planet, take the planet for a related hand (Two Pair, Three of a Kind, Full House; not Pluto) rather than nothing. That insures you against The Eye and The Mouth. Count it as a miss, not as progress, and never as a reason to open another pack.
- Targets: level 2-3 by the ante 2 boss (buy at least one main-hand planet before it), 3-5 by antes 3-4, 6-9 by antes 5-6. 'At target' means the target of the ante you are about to enter. With no xMult and the next ante below 30%, aim for level 5+ entering ante 5. Passing a Celestial pack at ante 4 because level 3 was 'inside 3-5', while ante 5 read 5-15%, left Pair at level 3 until death. Never let a second ante pass with the main hand at level 1. Once the hand is at target, planets stop counting as progress, so send the surplus toward xMult. While the board has no reliable xMult, do not keep building planet infrastructure for a hand already at target: $38 of Telescope and packs took Pair to level 8 while the outlook still showed a cliff.
- While below target: buy the main-hand planet on sight ($3-4). Take one Celestial look per shop before any joker reroll, and always buy the planet before a 2nd reroll in the same shop. When the hand is 2+ levels below target, single planets, Celestial packs ($4) and Telescope all come before rerolls. On a thin board under $10, a $3-4 planet beats a reroll or a second Buffoon pack. Cap rerolls at about $10 per ante unless you hold $60+. Below level 3 at ante 3, or below level 4 at ante 4, planets also come before holding interest above $25. Below about $15 with no way to reach $25 within the next ante, do not pass Telescope, a Celestial pack or Mercury to protect a tier. Take a Meteor Tag when it comes free, but do not skip a blind in antes 2-4 just for one.
- Reroll budget: if $10 of rerolls in one ante has not found an xMult, put the rest of the surplus into main-hand planets until the hand reaches target. Levels are certain progress; rerolls are a lottery.
- Celestial packs: buy them only to level the main hand. Once the main-hand planet shows up in shops, buy it there for $3 rather than chasing it through packs. Once two Celestial packs in a row miss the main-hand planet, stop buying them that ante and put the money into jokers or xMult rerolls: five packs for about $22 gave Jupiter and four Uranus. While below target, open a Celestial pack if you keep $20+ after it, or about $10-15 once $25 is covered, and nothing better is on offer. A voucher that fixes the run (Director's Cut) always comes first. Prefer packs to rerolls and to $6+ flat jokers and slow scalers. Buy Normal packs, not Mega, unless 2+ planets in the Mega pack are on-plan. Never open one that leaves you unable to fix the coming blind.
- If the main hand's planets have not shown up after two antes (by ante 3), switch to a drawable hand whose planets you keep being offered. If Pair jokers are on the board, that means Pair. If packs have already levelled another drawable hand while the main hand sits at level 1, set the style to that hand so the levels get used.
- Telescope and Planet Merchant pay off only when about 3+ Celestial packs will follow them, or with Constellation. When that is the plan and the main hand is committed, buy Telescope in antes 2-4 even if it costs one interest tier. Do not buy it for a hand already at target while the board still lacks xMult. Below target with no pack plan, spend that $10 on direct main-hand planets first. [seen in 37 games]
- Reroll limits:
- At most 2 rerolls per shop, and only 1 in an ante the outlook shows as safe. Spread them across shops. Never chain escalating rerolls ($5, $6, $7, $8) in one shop. Pay for a joker on offer rather than for more looks at the shop.
- When rerolling to save a failing blind, drop at most one interest tier per shop, and buy the certain upgrades already in the shop first (main-hand planet, Celestial pack). In ante 2, $34→$14 and $25→$14 of rerolls found only an eternal conditional Hack and a Bootstraps rental that the strategist then felt forced to buy.
- Set your buy bar before you reroll. If two rerolls in a row show only cheap scorers you pass on, the bar is too high: lower it and buy the best scorer instead of rerolling again. Nine rerolls ($51 over antes 3-4) once bought no joker at all.
- Never reroll if you could not then buy a $6-8 xMult on top of your floor. If two or three shops in a row turn up nothing, stop rerolling. Put the surplus into main-hand planets or rebuild money so the xMult can be bought when it appears.
- Antes 1-2: never reroll when it takes money below about $15. While one or two shops remain before the boss, do not reroll below $20 either. A low boss read early in the ante is not yet an emergency, so buy the cheap scorer on offer now. When the current ante reads 95-100%, do not reroll below $25. In ante 1 at 95%+ with under $20, do not reroll at all: a reroll at $15 (99%/95%) found only a Duo it did not buy. Exceptions: a single emergency reroll on an empty board before a blind (never chain a second one); and with 2+ empty slots while the next ante's boss reads below 30%, one $5 reroll per shop down to $15, after buying any lasting scorer on offer. Leave ante 1 with $10-15 so the ante 2 shops can buy two scorers.
- With a rental, keep at least rent + $4 after any reroll.
- In antes 1-2, never spend $15+ rerolling one shop.
- In a safe ante, do not reroll if it drops you below the next $5 interest tier.
- Once 2 lasting scorers exist, never reroll below $20 unless the NEXT blind or the current ante's boss reads below 70%. While every blind of the current ante reads 95%+, never reroll below $25 ($28 with a rental), whatever the forecast for later antes says. The severe-forecast exception releases money for planets, Buffoon packs and empty-slot scorers, not for rerolls. Buy the certain upgrades before any reroll.
- If the main hand is below its level target, take a Celestial look first and cap rerolls at about $10 per ante.
- Buy money-scaling jokers (Bull, Bootstraps) only if you will really hold $25+, and never under $20. Do not buy them on a plan that spends heavily on rerolls or rentals, or while the engine is still being bought. A core Bootstraps made the strategist refuse a boss counter, and the run lost to The Club. While you own one, check the next-blind outlook after each spend. Stop if it would fall below about 85% or drop more than 5 points.
- From ante 3, reroll only with money above $25 ($28 with a rental, $31 with two), and only if you can open a slot: know which joker you would sell before you reroll. Below $20 at ante 3+, do not reroll at all unless the next blind reads below 70%.
- Stop once one shop has used about $20 on rerolls. Never pay $8-10 for a reroll unless you hold $60+.
Never rerolling at all is also a failure. A run that rerolled once all game, leaving shops at $14-22 with empty slots while the next ante read 0-25%, lost. While the board has fewer than 2 multipliers, use 1-2 $5 rerolls per shop with money above the floor, in the early shops of the ante rather than the boss shop. If the boss itself is the problem, first look for a fix aimed at that boss. [seen in 27 games]
- Rentals and debt. A rental's real price is $3 times the rounds you will keep it (about 20 rounds from ante 2, so about $15-20+ even for a $1 rental), not its sticker. Before buying one, money after the purchase should be at least $3 × the rounds until you could sell it, plus $5. A rental also raises the money floor to $28, which blocks rerolls for the rest of the run.
Ante 1: buy no rentals, even at $1 or as a free pack pick, unless the current blind fails without one. The other exceptions:
- The board has no scoring joker and either the ante's boss reads below about 90% or ante 2's Small Blind reads below about 50%. Then a rental that scores now (e.g. Half Joker on Pair) beats a scaler that starts at 0.
- You hold an xMult with no base. Then a big flat-chips rental (Stuntman +250) or an affordable Bootstraps is worth it.
Ante 2: buy a rental only if the current blind reads below about 50% and no non-rental option fixes it, or under the lasting-scaler exception below. Antes 3-4: buy one only if the next blind reads below 70% without it, or under one of the exceptions. Carry at most one rental in antes 2-4. A flat scoring rental bought while the ante reads 90%+ is never worth it. Never take a rental for flat Mult when a non-rental fix exists. Never take a money-scaling rental (Bull, Bootstraps) in antes 1-4 unless you will really keep $28+, even when it is free. Never take a new rental, or a second one, below $20. Bootstraps (eternal rental) bought at $14 and Shoot the Moon (eternal rental, no Queens in the deck) at $9 left $8 against $6 a round of rent, and every later buy lowered the boss read. A Half Joker rental at $6 followed by Ramen as a second rental at $9 went into -$5 debt. From ante 3, one lasting rental that is a core scorer for the main hand is acceptable only with a free slot and only if you still hold $28 after buying it. If a second rental is the only survival fix, sell one at the first shop where the next blind reads 85-90%+ without it, before money hits $0. Never hold two rentals below $28, and never carry two across an ante below $31.
Lasting-scaler exception (Yellow Deck): from ante 2, with $25+ in hand and the next boss safe, one rental that is a lasting xMult or a scaler you will really feed (Hologram; Green Joker played with zero discards) is acceptable. Hold $28 afterwards.
xMult exception: from ante 2, if the board has no xMult and an upcoming boss reads below 50%, an affordable rental xMult that fires on every main-hand play (Cavendish, Card Sharp on a repeated hand, Baseball with Uncommons, Acrobat, Vampire) beats any flat +Mult option. Accept an eternal rental only for such an every-hand xMult when nothing sellable is available. Never use the exception for a periodic or conditional xMult. Refuse it too if you already carry a rental.
Eternal rentals: never buy one for anything except that every-hand xMult. It charges $3 every round for the rest of the run. A $1 eternal rental Banner kept money at $1-17 for the rest of the run.
Always:
- With a rental, the floor is $28, not $25. Never spend to $0 while holding one.
- Never use Credit Card or debt to pay for scoring in antes 1-3. At $0 or below, buy no rentals.
- Never take a rental that is perishable or decaying (Popcorn, Ice Cream, Ramen), even as a free pack pick. If you hold one, sell it the shop before it expires: a perishable rental Mystic Summit taken on an empty board at ante 1 kept charging $3 a round after it was debuffed. Never carry a third rental.
- Sell a survival rental as soon as the blind you rented it for is behind you, unless the outlook shows you still need it.
- Do not let the $28/$31 floor block buys that improve the build.
- Before a boss that costs money (The Tooth), enter with cash for the cards you expect to play + $3 per rental + $5. [seen in 26 games]
- Interest against forecasts (once 2 lasting scorers exist; before that, the survival rule applies). Hold $25 only once the board already passes the next ante. Drop below $25 ($28 with a rental) for survival only when the next blind or the current ante's boss reads below about 70%. In antes 2-5 the forecast for the NEXT ante, read off the current board, is almost always bad. On its own it never justifies spending down every ante or rerolling below $25. A high outlook that rests on a variable joker, or a boss that hides information, is no reason to spend the bank either. While the current ante reads 95%+ in antes 2-4, do not buy speculative packs, off-plan jokers whose trigger the main hand never makes, or random Arcana that take you below $25. Do not open a pack unless you will take a pick from it. $27 went to $11 in ante 2 on a Buffoon pack with every card skipped, a perishable Superposition on a Two Pair plan, and a random Wheel of Fortune, and antes 3-4 ran at $3-14. From ante 4, while the current ante reads 95%+, spend only the surplus above $25 ($28 with a rental) and never drop below $20.
Severe-forecast exception, which applies especially with no xMult. A cliff one ante away is an emergency now, not when you reach it, but it releases money only for certain upgrades, never for extra rerolls:
- Next ante's boss below about 50%: spend down to the $25 tier in every shop of the current ante.
- Next ante's boss or Big Blind below about 30%, any blind of the next ante below about 20%, or the board's only xMult is perishable and expires within the next ante: the interest floor no longer applies to certain upgrades. Add at least one in each shop of the current ante: a main-hand planet, a Celestial pack while below target, a Buffoon pack, or a lasting scorer for the played hand in an empty slot. If the main hand is 3+ levels below target, related-hand planets and Planet Merchant count too. Spend down to about $10-15 plus $3 per rental. The floor protects money for certain upgrades; it never means buying nothing. Runs that left shops at $11-22 with empty slots while the next ante read 0-25% passed Uranus, Mars, Square Joker, Red Card and Zany to protect a self-made floor, and died.
- Rerolls under the exception: while every blind of the current ante reads 95%+, reroll only with money above $25 (at most 2 per shop), and only after the certain upgrades are bought. The empty-slot reroll allowance in the reroll rule also applies. If the outlook has shown the next ante at 0-10% for two antes in a row, the build lacks a multiplier. Start $5 xMult rerolls and Buffoon packs from that surplus. If three shops in a row miss, stop rerolling and rebuild to the price of an xMult ($6-10).
Act in the current ante's shops that still have a blind after them, while rerolls still cost $5. Do not save the money for the dying ante. Spend only on things that directly add xMult, main-hand levels or, in an empty slot, score on the played hand. Spectral and random Arcana packs and one-card tarots do not count as fixing a forecast, except an Arcana aimed at a named edit on trigger cards. Do not dump the money into escalating rerolls in one shop.
When the boss is below 50% and you dip into survival money, judge each $ by how much it raises the boss estimate. Prefer a main-hand planet already in the shop, then joker rerolls. If two buys in a row miss, stop and keep the interest. [seen in 21 games]
- Unreliable scoring is backup, not the plan. That includes perishable jokers (Space, Banner, Wrathful when perishable), decaying ones (Ice Cream, Popcorn, Seltzer, Turtle Bean), random ones (Misprint), time-limited ones (Seltzer, Ramen) and destroyable ones (Gros Michel). Every one you hold is a slot that must be refilled later. From ante 3, pick a lasting scorer even if it scores less right now. A board of Space, Popcorn, Banner and Wrathful lost all four by ante 4 and was left with three weak jokers.
- Count a perishable as a scorer only for the blinds it will still be alive for, usually the current ante. If it expires before the first failing blind, the problem is not solved: keep searching for a permanent xMult and keep money ready for it.
- When a perishable xMult is the board's main multiplier, count its rounds on the day you take it. Plan its replacement to arrive at least one shop before expiry. Never 'keep interest' while a perishable carries the board.
- Hold at most 2 perishables at once. Once 2 are on the board, the next joker bought must be a lasting one. Never replace an expiring perishable with another perishable, or sell a lasting scorer to buy one, unless the current blind fails without it.
- When checking a boss two or more blinds ahead, count a decaying joker at what it will be worth by then and a perishable that expires first as zero. By ante 3, have at least 2 scoring jokers that do not shrink. If a bridge is the only fix, buy it, but the next spend goes to something lasting.
- Do not pay $5 for a shrinking joker when it leaves you under $5, unless the current blind fails without it.
- Never let two perishables expire in the same ante or right at a boss.
- When the danger is 1-2 antes out and the current ante reads 80%+, two cases apply:
  (a) Do not churn stopgaps. Stopgaps bought and sold one shop later drained $50 to $18. Do not let them take the money or slot meant for xMult, main-hand planets or deck shaping.
  (b) With an empty slot and the next ante below about 30%, do not turn down a joker that scores on the played hand only because of its sticker, within the 2-perishable cap. Buy it if it will still be alive at the failing blind.
- Replace a shrinking chips joker before it falls to about half its value.
- From ante 3, treat a flat joker that scores under 10% of the hand as a slot to free.
- If more than half the board's scoring is unreliable, work out the bad case and keep buying lasting scoring until the boss clears without those pieces.
- Never let a perishable or rental joker be your only chips source. [seen in 21 games]
- In antes 1-2, survival beats interest until two conditions hold: the board has 2 lasting, unconditional scoring jokers (+Mult or chips that fire on ordinary hands), and the main hand is level 2 or higher. Survival means every blind of the current ante, including its boss. Treat a boss reading below about 85% as a failing blind, even if the next blind reads 97%. Also judge ante 1 buys by the ante 2 boss read, not only by the next blind. When the current blind already reads 95%+ and the boss is safe too, do not pay for perishable, decaying or off-plan jokers, packs or rerolls. Until those 2 scorers are in place:
- Do not leave a shop holding $15+ while a blind of this ante is failing. Spend down to about $10. In ante 1, with fewer than 2 unconditional scorers, do not leave a shop at $12+ without buying an affordable unconditional +Mult or chips joker. A suit-conditional joker (Greedy) does not count. Before the main hand is fixed, a scorer for the hand the round player really plays (Clever while Two Pair is being played) is acceptable. Leaving ante 1 shops at $14 and $23 with only Greedy gave a 5% Flint. In ante 1, go below $10 only if a blind of this ante would fail, or if the next ante's Small Blind already reads below about 30%. In that case buy direct scorers or main-hand planets down to about $5-8. Never finish ante 1 under $10 otherwise.
- Direct scorers first. In antes 1-3, buy the cheapest certain scorer, check the outlook again, and pay for packs or rerolls only from money above $15. Never let one shop take a $20+ bank under $10 on gambles. $22 went to $3 on a reroll and two Celestial packs that missed; the next shop's $4 Green Joker took The Head from 15% to 94%, and money stayed at $1-11 for the rest of the run.
- Take a joker that scores now over a scaler that starts at 0 (e.g. Red Card), even if the scorer is a rental (see the rentals rule).
- An early conditional xMult (The Idol, The Duo) is a finisher, not a base. Until there is one unconditional +Mult or chips joker or a levelled main hand, rank cheap unconditional scorers and main-hand planets above conditional or perishable jokers.
- Cheap +Mult stopgaps (Jolly, Raised Fist, Gros Michel, or any perishable) are a bridge only when the current blind fails without them. Otherwise take a non-perishable scorer even if it is slightly weaker. Never let two stopgaps expire in the same ante or right at a boss.
- Use the Yellow Deck head start on Buffoon packs only as part of a plan to reach $25 by ante 3. The extra $10 pays for one early pack, not a pack plus a reroll plus a buy. In ante 1, open one only if you could still afford a shop joker or a reroll after a miss.
- Every joker slot and pack pick goes to scoring. Do not take utility or economy jokers (Drunkard, Chaos, Splash, Business Card, Hallucination, Mail-In Rebate, To the Moon, Cloud 9, Certificate) or a $10 voucher like Grabber. In antes 1-2 a Buffoon pack with no scorer is a skip, so take nothing rather than a free non-scorer. A free Drunkard became a crutch that Banner later depended on.
- Zero scoring jokers before any blind from the ante 1 Big Blind on is an emergency. Buy any affordable scorer. If there is none, do one $5 reroll, then open an Arcana pack (Judgement). Never enter a blind with an empty board while holding $10+.
- With no scoring jokers, play for the biggest base hand you can draw (see the in-blind pace rule) and take pack jokers that pay off now (Runner over Certificate).
- An early xMult (e.g. Card Sharp) must be followed at once by an unconditional base joker and a main-hand planet.
- Take a value generator only when the next boss is safe by the conservative check.
Once the 2 lasting scorers are in place, bank: aim for $25 by the end of ante 2, and hold $25 from ante 3. [seen in 18 games]
- Eternal jokers are a permanent slot cost. Before any Eternal buy, ask: 'when the xMult shows up, which slot does it go in?'
- Accept an Eternal sticker only on an xMult or an unconditional scorer for the main hand that you would keep to ante 8. Never on a conditional joker (Hack), a joker whose trigger you lack (Shoot the Moon without Queens), or a rental economy joker (Bootstraps). Four Eternals (Hack, Bootstraps, Half Joker, Shoot the Moon) left only Greedy sellable by ante 4, and the only possible change was a perishable swap.
- Before ante 5, lock at most one slot with a non-xMult Eternal, and only for a scaler or scorer that fits the main hand and does not fight the rest of the board. Never hold more than 2 non-xMult Eternals at any point.
- From ante 3, while the board has no xMult, keep at least one slot free or sellable for it. Buy no new non-xMult Eternal then. Never sell a key Mult source for an Eternal utility joker.
- On a near-empty board (3+ free slots) with a failing forecast before ante 4, the first Eternal scorer for the played hand costs little: do not turn it down for the sticker.
- Never take an Eternal flat or conditional +Mult or chips joker, or an Eternal utility joker, if it would make 2+ Eternal slots, even when it is free from a pack. The only exception is a next blind below 50% without it, with nothing else that fixes it.
- Keep at least 2 non-eternal slots you can sell or swap through ante 4 and beyond, so the convert-to-xMult step stays possible.
- If a blind forces a third Eternal, take the one with the highest ceiling (an xMult, Hanging Chad, a retrigger), not flat Mult.

DRAW PILE: 24 cards; suits Spades 7, Hearts 4, Clubs 9, Diamonds 3; ranks 3:3, 4:1, 5:1, 6:3, 7:1, 9:1, 10:4, Jack:4, King:3, Ace:2

JOKERS (numbered for grow_joker, left to right):
  1. Blackboard (X3 Mult if all cards held in hand are Spades or Clubs)
  2. Photograph [holo; rental] (First played face card gives X2 Mult when scored)
  3. Seeing Double [eternal] (X2 Mult if played hand has a scoring Club card and a scoring card of any other suit)
  4. Brainstorm (Copies the ability of leftmost Joker)
  5. Wily Joker [eternal] (+100 Chips if played hand contains a Three of a Kind)

CONSUMABLES: The World (Converts up to 3 selected cards to Spades)

HAND LEVELS (level, times played): High Card lvl 3 (8x), Pair lvl 1 (9x), Two Pair lvl 3 (9x), Three of a Kind lvl 1 (3x), Straight lvl 1 (3x), Flush lvl 1 (2x), Full House lvl 1 (1x), Four of a Kind lvl 1 (1x)

CURRENT STYLE: none

ESTIMATE (the round player, over many possible draws): playing on clears this blind about 0% of the time; using The World now (on the engine's own choice of target cards) about 0%.

YOUR PLAN NOTE: This is last-ditch survival at ante 7. Keep Blackboard leftmost so Brainstorm copies it. Use The World on red cards held in hand so the held cards are all Spades or Clubs. Play Two Pair or High Card (the levelled hands) with Clubs scoring for Seeing Double. Play trips when they can be drawn so Wily's chips fire. If we survive, spend every dollar on Two Pair/High Card planets or flat chips. Sell the Photograph rental only when a replacement is affordable.

LEGAL MOVES:
0. Play on: the round player makes the next play or discard (following your style)
1. Use The World now (Converts up to 3 selected cards to Spades)

Answer with your reasoning, the move number, the target card numbers (for a tarot or spectral that needs them, else []) and the style for the rest of the round.

answer.reasoning: Only one hand is left, with no discards, and 22,784 is still needed. The best play is Two Pair AA KK, holding the four Clubs: 102 chips × 204 Mult (Photograph x2, Blackboard x3, holo +10, Seeing Double x2, Brainstorm x3) is about 20,800, still short. A Club Flush after The World scores only about 13,700. There are not enough Spades for a Spade Flush. Using The World before the Two Pair adds nothing.
